name: Say It Like a Creed
why_it_works: People don't just buy from brands; they join them. A short creed of 'We are the kind of people who...' lines gives fans a shared identity they can repeat, tag friends with and wear. Identity statements outlast offers because people defend who they are.

hook.pattern: Open on a single declarative identity line, spoken like a vow, with no product in sight.
examples: We are the kind of people who {{creed_line_one}}.
Not a team. A creed. Here it is.
If you {{creed_line_one}}, you're already one of us.

variables.name: brand
variables.description: Team, club, shop or brand name

variables.name: creed_line_one
variables.description: First identity line, an action they take
variables.example: fix it ourselves before we pay to fix it

variables.name: creed_line_two
variables.example: wave at every lowrider, chrome or primer

variables.name: creed_line_three
variables.example: bring the kids to every show

variables.name: refusal_line
variables.description: One thing the group never does

variables.name: gathering
variables.description: Where fans can show up or belong
variables.example: Sunday cruise night on Mission Avenue

craft.notes: Repeat the same opening ('Who...') so the lines feel like a chant and are easy to quote in comments. Every line must be an action, not an adjective: 'bring the kids' beats 'family-friendly'. The refusal line gives the creed teeth.

do_not: Write lines that exclude people for who they are rather than what they do
Show street racing, unsafe stunts or alcohol with driving
